headline: This law requires federal agencies to set up better evaluation and public reporting for most US foreign aid programs.
what_it_does: The law defines which US foreign aid counts as covered, including development assistance, Economic Support Fund aid, Millennium Challenge Act programs, and Food for Peace programs. Within 18 months, the President must issue guidelines telling agencies how to set goals, measure results, collect data, and evaluate programs, and must give Congress a detailed description of those guidelines. The State Department must also update its ForeignAssistance.gov website within 90 days with program, budget, and spending information, and agencies must send it quarterly data. Agencies can withhold specific information from the website if they tell Congress in writing that publishing it would harm people, security, or proprietary interests.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that administer foreign aid, such as the State Department and USAID
who_it_affects.how: They must follow new presidential guidelines on setting goals, evaluating programs, and reporting results, and they must send program data to the State Department each quarter.

who_it_affects.group: Implementing partners and organizations that carry out US-funded foreign aid projects
who_it_affects.how: Information about their awards and projects will be published online, though agencies may withhold details that could endanger people or reveal proprietary information.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public and researchers interested in foreign aid spending
who_it_affects.how: They can view award-level, country-level, and regional information, budget documents, and evaluations on ForeignAssistance.gov.

who_it_affects.group: Program beneficiaries in countries receiving US foreign aid
who_it_affects.how: Their safety may be considered when agencies decide whether certain program details should be published online.

when_it_takes_effect: The State Department website update is due within 90 days of enactment on July 15, 2016, and presidential guidelines are due within 18 months. The bill also expresses a sense of Congress that State and USAID should coordinate data collection by the end of fiscal year 2018.
